answer: Random cohorts with joint liability: each new identity posts a 20 POA bond and a public beacon places it in a cohort of five strangers; the cohort atlas is published. Members can read each other's signing logs and file a cipher-signed duplicate report. If an audit later proves a member is a clone, members who did not report lose half their bonds and the reporter collects them. Clones land among strangers paid to expose them, so each extra identity buys another bond and more watchers. Limit: a farm that floods a quiet tundra of sign-ups can fill whole cohorts with its own clones.
